summary: Tuberculosis still kills over a million people a year, and portable ultrasound could screen for it in rural clinics, but there are few labelled lung scans. Every one beat their earlier system, and when set to catch 90 of 100 sick patients, correct all-clear results for healthy people rose from about 60 to 79 of 100. Surprisingly, which network they borrowed barely mattered: the small amount of labelled data is the real bottleneck.

summary: A simple 'allowed tools' list is too weak to keep an AI agent safe, because what is safe depends on what it already did. When an attacker fully takes over the agent, Sapien blocked about 93–95 of every 100 attacks on one benchmark, against about 83–87 for a plain allowed list, while normal tasks almost always still worked.

summary: Radio telescope arrays do not take pictures: they measure scattered samples of the image's 2D Fourier transform, and astronomers must fill in the rest. The AI models were about 5% better on typical cases, up to 15% better near Cameroon and Gabon one day ahead, but worse in dry highland areas.

They also found that the 'heat maps' meant to explain the network's decisions became close to random on lens-free images unless smoothed.

summary: Flash floods can form in under six hours, often where there are few rain gauges. TACLS uses GPS ground stations that already exist: water vapour in the air slightly delays the satellite signals, so the delay tells you how much moisture is overhead. A machine-learning model trained on over 30 years of these readings flags sudden moisture jumps and separates real storms from glitches, and forecasters then decide whether to warn. In tests on past storms it caught about 93 of every 100 flash-flood warnings that were issued, and it is due at all 122 US weather offices in the second half of October.
techniques: Anomaly detection on long time series

terms.meaning: Satellite navigation systems like GPS; ground receivers record signals from them all day.
Moist air slows radio waves a tiny bit, so the extra travel time reveals how much water is in the air.
Teaching a model what normal looks like, so it can flag anything unusual.

title: NWS Deploys Improved TACLS to 122 Offices for Earlier Flash Flood Warnings

authors: E. Nikolaou, M. W. Eckhoff, … D. Aspinall

summary: AI assistants that can send emails, pay bills or book travel can be tricked by hidden instructions planted in a web page or a message. This team checks the assistant's whole plan before it is allowed to touch anything. They turn the plan into a small state machine and use a model checker, the same kind of tool used to prove chips correct, to test it against written safety rules. On a standard test suite, their rules fully covered 22 of 28 security policies, and when a plan fails the check, the tool shows the assistant exactly why so it can fix the plan.
techniques: Turning code into a state machine
Feeding the failure trace back to the AI to repair its plan

A precise way to write rules about order in time, like 'money is never sent before the user approves'.

This team built a calibrated test setup from a programmable radio and measured 16 people at six frequencies between 10 and 22.5 GHz.
